sample_size.excerpt: A total of 14,203 men aged 40 to 69 years who had returned the baseline questionnaire and provided blood samples were observed from 1990 to 2005. During a mean of 12.8 years of follow-up, 201 newly diagnosed prostate cancers were identified.

cases.excerpt: During a mean of 12.8 years of follow-up, 201 newly diagnosed prostate cancers were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Although plasma daidzein showed no association, the highest tertile for plasma equol, a metabolite of daidzein, was significantly associated with a decreased risk of total prostate cancer (OR = 0.60; 95% CI, 0.36 to 0.99; P(trend) = .04). These inverse associations were strengthened after analysis was confined to localized cases, with ORs in the highest group of plasma genistein and equol compared with the lowest of 0.54 (95% CI, 0.29 to 1.01; P(trend) = .03) and 0.43 (95% CI, 0.22 to 0.82; P(trend) = .02), respectively.
